summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog executes arbitrary commands from remote server and auto-upgrades globally
details: The `tt-help watchdog` subcommand starts a long-running agent that POSTs heartbeats to a server URL read from `~/.tt-help.json` (README example http://117.71.53.99:17301, plain HTTP, bare IP) and parses `data.commands` from each response, splitting each string and passing it to `child_process.spawn(command, args, { shell: IS_WIN })` with auto-restart on crash. Whoever controls that server has full-host command execution on every machine running the watchdog. The same loop runs `child_process.exec('npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest')` from `performUpgrade()` on a 10-minute timer and on remote signal, providing a persistent global-install update channel with no version pinning or integrity check. Each heartbeat also sends hostname, non-internal IPv4 address, OS/arch/release, CPU list, memory stats, Node version, load averages, client config, and a list of running child processes with PIDs and RSS to the same endpoint. The default server is a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint over plain HTTP; the command channel is not the documented purpose of a CLI help tool and is not directed at operator-configured infrastructure by default.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
